Commentary.Commentary: 'Never judge a pitch till both the sides have bowled on it,' goes the saying. True. But in this case, Australia are well, well short. They are short of runs, short of fit bowlers, short of self-confidence... they might need to bowl really well to even make a match out of this. Join us back at 1735 local (0735 GMT) for the second session.

Once again, England have done well with the ball. Yes, the field is big and the outfield not the quickest but the bowling was excellent. They have found ways to stall Australia even when the latter were going strong. Joe Root started the collapse, if one might add, for Australia. He dismissed Steven Smith and Travis Head in quick succession and that left the hosts struggling to score quickly. Rashid then broke the 85-run stand between Finch and Marsh, getting the latter and Stoinis in the space of 6 balls. Towards the end, the seamers were excellent, not giving anything away.

This innings almost was a replica of the previous match. Just a slight difference being the openers providing a decent start. Aaron Finch once again failed to make his century count, Smith and Marsh could not convert their starts and then some decent hitting at the death saving their face. My colleague KingVic sums it up correctly - Australia are about 80 runs short.

Disappointing performance from Australia again. They were 161/3 in 30 overs and going by David Lloyd's theory, teams usually double that by the 50-over mark. At least, with those many wickets left. But they have managed just 109 runs in the last 20 overs, losing 6 wickets. If we dissect further, just 57/5 in the last 10.

OUT! A run out to end the innings. A short ball around off, nicely taking the pace off, Tye looks to pull but is cramped for room. gets a bottom edge onto his body and the ball rolls to the leg side. The batsmen go for the single but Woakes quickly gets to the ball, turns around, takes aim and bang. Hits the stumps at the bowler's end. AUSTRALIA END ON 270/9.

SIX! BOSH! A number 10 hits a six! Just the third of the innings, after Finch and Smith hit one each. A full toss on middle, Tye swings it cleanly over long on and just about clears the leaping fielder!
Another short ball outside off, Andrew swings hard but misses.
A short ball outside off, Tye pulls it over mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and outside off, hit through mid on for a single.
Andrew Tye walks in at number 10, replacing Starc.

OUT! Caught this time. And the fielder is Jason Roy. A length ball on middle and leg, Starc backs away and swings it over mid-wicket. Again, he does not have enough on it and finds the fielder at mid-wicket near the fence. Hang on... Roy misjudges it too! However, he adjusts well, running back late and just about taking it near his head.

DROPPED! What happened there? Did the sun get into Root's eyes? Somehow, he has missed a fairly simple chance. A short ball, on middle, Starc pulls this over mid-wicket. It looks a good hit but this ground is so big that it does not have enough legs to travel beyond the fielder at the boundary. Joe Root runs to his right, but then perhaps does not see the ball clearly. Because he overruns it. He then sticks out his left hand, perhaps because he sees the ball at the last moment. Prevents what would have been an embarrassing six. Just a single.
A short ball around off, Cameron pulls it through mid-wicket for one more.
Another one on the hips, Mitchell tucks it through square leg and White looks for two but Starc shouts, 'NO! NO! NO!' Just a single then.
Another pull, just one.
Down the leg side, Starc backs away and works it through square leg for a run.
A short ball on middle, pulled away through square leg for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. Terrific over - 1, 0, 0, W, 0, 0.
Down the leg side, Starc misses his tuck and the ball goes off his pads towards short third man.
Mitchell Starc comes in.

OUT! The dive has not saved Carey! That is why you should play other sports as well. Football has helped Woakes in cricket. On a length outside off, White looks to pull but gets a thick inside edge onto his body. Carey calls for the single but has to run around Woakes as the bowler too dashes for the ball. Kicks it onto the stumps and Carey dives. It is referred upstairs but replays show that it is not enough. Australia still in with a shout to get bowled out before the 300th legal ball.
Direct hit! Has Carey timed his dive to perfection?
Backs away to the leg side a year in advance and Woakes bowls it wide outside off. The Bear cannot reach.
Gets across his stumps and Woakes bowls it on middle, White looks to swing it over the keeper but misses. Seems like the ball hits his pads but England appeal for the catch. Not given.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Chris Woakes is back on.
Walks down the track and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
A short ball on middle, Carey backs away and looks to pull but misses. Seemed like a slower one, but dear me, the speed gun says 141.8 kph!
The batsman plays a pull shot to this short delivery. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Banged in short, pulled away for a run.
A short ball, delivered from wide of the crease, White looks to pull but is cramped for room. Gets a bottom edge through mid-wicket and it is a single.
Full and outside off, driven sweetly through the covers for a couple.

FOUR! Lovely shot. Full and outside off, Carey reaches out and lofts it over covers for a boundary! That is 11 from the over and the last 2 have spoilt the figures for Rashid. He ends with 10-0-71-2, with 23 coming off the last 2.
Driven towards the mid off region. They pick up a single.
Comes down the track, but is not to the pitch of the ball. Defends it to the off side.
Short and on the stumps, Alex punches it towards point and sets off for the quick run. The fielder gets to the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Would have been tight.
FOUR! BOOM! Full and outside off, Carey gets down and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket for a boundary!
Full and outside off, White reverse paddles it through short third man for a single.
Works this through mid-wicket and gets one. Just 4 from this over.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
On middle and leg, pushed back to the bowler. Another dot.
The ball has found the edge of the bat. They pick up a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On middle and leg, pushed back to the bowler.
Mark Wood is back.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single. 12 from the over, some momentum for the Aussies.
WIDE. Well played from Carey. He stands outside leg, sees the ball outside leg, then calmly gets across, shouldering arms.

Now White shows how the reverse sweep is played but how good a fielding is that from Buttler? The ball bounces onto the pitch but Buttler sticks his right leg out and just deflects the ball towards the off side. Just a run, when it could have been many more. 'He has saved a goal!' says Michael Clarke on air.

Now he goes for the reverse sweep but due to the extra bounce, the ball goes off his gloves, just past Jos Buttler. Seemed like there was two available as Chris Woakes had a fairly decent ground to cover from short third man. But only a single taken.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for Carey! Rashid floats this around leg and this time the southpaw paddles it fine past the keeper!
FOUR! Better shot from Carey. Uses his big reach, gets down to the pitch of the ball and sweeps it through square leg for a boundary.
Landed outside off, it is the googly and it has bamboozled Carey. Tamely pushes inside the line and is beaten.
And a forward defense to end the over. Terrific over from Plunkett. So far, Australia have scored 8/2 in 3 Powerplay 3 overs.
On middle and leg, another one goes off the inner half of the bat through mid-wicket. This time for a single.
Another dot. Full on middle and leg, pushed off the inner half of the bat straight back to the bowler.
Outside off, punched straight to point.
WIDE. Full and down the leg side, Carey misses his flick.
No run there again. Pushed back to the bowler.
Outside off, punched through the covers but straight to the fielder.
Now he gets the sweep right and earns a single through square leg. 3 runs and a wicket from that over.
Full and outside off, Alex looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. Bounce.
Now the paddle from White and he earns a run.
And he is away first ball. Outside of, Carey goes back and just opens the face of his bat to guide it to short third man for a single.
Time for one of the debutants. Alex Carey walks in at number 8, with Australia under threat of being bowled out. Forget 350, they may just scrape past 250.

OUT! That is a terrific catch! Jos Buttler dropped a tough one earlier in the day but this is a magnificent take. Tossed up outside off, Stoinis stays leg side of the ball and looks to drive this inside out but the ball turns away just a shade and takes a thin outside edge. Buttler collects it cleanly and does not even bother to whip the bails, as is a normal keeper's habit. He then appeals and up goes the umpire's finger! The Aussies have now lost 3 wickets for 7 runs in the last 13 balls!
Full on middle, pushed straight back.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.
WIDE. Down the leg side again, this time it is wided as White gets across.
Gets across his stumps and Plunkett ducks in a bouncer on middle, the Bear then ducks.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Cameron White eventually walks out at a bat. Not quite the position for him, IMHO.

OUT! Perfect. Following the template to the 'T'. Score quickly in the Mandatory Powerplay, then slow down, jog across to a ton and then throw it away. Aaron Finch does it time and again. Full on middle and off, the intention is correct from Finch, looking to go over the top but perhaps he could have waited an over or two. Marsh was just dismissed. And now Australia have lost 2 in quick succession. Plunkett wraps his fingers around the ball and as a result, it comes on much slower than Finch's anticipation. He is through with his lofted shot pretty early and the ball goes off the inner half of the bat, straight to Jason Roy at mid on. He escaped a similar chance a few overs go when he cleared mid on. Still, for the numbers, a good score by Finch. He has made a century, but might still find his team on the losing side. Meanwhile, PLUNKETT HAS GOT TO 100 ODI WICKETS.
POWERPLAY 3 time. 5 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the end of the innings.
Full and down the leg side, paddled fine for a couple. Having conceded 19 in his first 2 overs, this has been an excellent comeback from Rashid. Just 26 in his last 5.
Fullish, on middle, swept through the leg side for a single.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket.
Gets off the mark straightaway, with a tuck through the leg side for a single.
Marcus Stoinis finally comes out to bat at number 6, replacing Marsh. Stoinis recently made a 99 against the Brisbane Heat, playing for Melbourne Stars in the BBL, at this very ground.

OUT! Stumped by a mile. Marsh jumps down the track, perhaps giving the signal in 2017 and Rashid is quick to spot that. Slows the flight, gives it a bit more loop, throws the ball wide outside off and Marsh misses his swing. Buttler does not miss the ball behind and comfortably takes the bails off. Another start not converted by Marsh and this could be dangerous for Australia. They would have wanted him at the crease in the death overs. End of a good stand but not necessarily devastating for England.
Outside off, pushed to the off side for a quick single.
Outside off, tapped to the off side. Mitchell wants a single but Jos Buttler quickly gets to the ball and the batsman is sent back.
FOUR! Not quite hit well but he has got enough. A short ball, Marsh goes back and heaves it in the air, wide of the man running to his left from deep mid-wicket and into the fence.
On off, worked through mid-wicket for a single. The stand is now worth 80 from 90 balls.
Aaarggghhhh! That is the grunt from Plunkett as soon as he delivers the ball. It is angled down the leg side and Finch misses his flick. Wide called.
Excellent running. Full on middle, AF flicks it through mid-wicket and runs hard for the second.
Full and wide outside off, Aaron swings hard but misses.
Outside off, Finch mistimes his cut towards point. Gets a bottom edge. Wants the run but is sent back.
Liam Plunkett is back on.
Short and outside off, punched behind point for a couple. 200 UP FOR AUSTRALIA! They need at least another 150 from the remaining 12 overs.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Full on middle, pushed to the bowler.

10th ODI ton for Finch, 5th against England! Equals Ricky Ponting's tally of tons against England, most by an Aussie! Down the leg side, Finch works this through square leg, calls for two and then makes Mitchell Marsh run hard for the second. What a glorious week for the opener. Struggled in the Big Bash to no end and here, two matches, two centuries. Takes his helmet off, shows off that chewing gum, then raises his arms in celebration. Australia would want a win tonight and hope for him to continue.
Another dot. Finch flicks it, but straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and down the leg side, there comes the paddle and again, it is straight to short fine leg.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
A short ball on middle, pulled away for a single.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.
The batsman fails to get bat on that one and is hit on the pad. They pick up a single. Leg bye given by the umpire.
On a good length outside off, defended solidly.
Some issue with the ball. Morgan shows it to the umpire and the latter cuts off the leather.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Full on middle, another sweep, straight to short fine leg.

FOUR! Better shot from Finch and he finds the boundary! Full and on middle, Finch gets down and sweeps it powerfully through mid-wicket. There are two men in the deep, one from square leg and the other at mid-wicket, both come, the latter dives but cannot stop the ball!
Full and down the leg side, Finch paddles it away but straight to short fine leg. That man has been very handy today. Not even conceded a single run.
Now the drive through mid off for a run.
Full on middle, pushed through mid on for a single.
The batsman plays a pull shot to this short delivery. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A short ball on middle, pulled away for a single.

Interesting awareness! Mitchell pushes it to the off side and then is just about to pick the ball and hand it to the keeper. But then realizes that recently, in the Under-19 World Cup, a South African batsman had done the same. The fielding side, Windies, had appealed then and he was adjudged out! Marsh then withdraws his hand.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
On middle and leg, worked through the leg side for a run.
Full and outside off, driven straight back for a single.
DRINKS BREAK...
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a couple.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On middle, punched through mid on for a single.
Full and on middle, swept through square leg for a couple.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Adil Rashid is back on.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
A short ball, Marsh heaves this through mid-wicket for just a run.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
WIDE. An attempted bouncer which was well over head height. The Umpire signals a wide.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A short ball outside off, Marsh looks to pull but misses.
Chris Woakes into the attack now.
Full and down the leg side, Aaron looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. There is an appeal for LBW but it is so bad that even the umpire smiles. Pitched MILES outside leg.
A tad short on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for one more.
Works this through square leg for a run.
A tad short, Marsh finally gets this one away, punching it past short extra cover to long off for a single.
Comes down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards square leg.
Outside off, Finch looks to cut but misses.
Pulls this through mid-wicket for three.
The ball has struck the batsman hard on his hand. Extra bounce.
On middle, Marsh punches this down the ground, where mid on is pretty deep but no single taken.
Outside off, tapped to the off side for a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and on middle, swept away for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Finch rocks back and punches it through the covers. Still no one in the deep for the spinners on the off side.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side. They pick up a single.
Down the leg side, clipped fine for a single.
FOUR! That is dropped short and Marsh is onto it in a flash. Pulls it through mid-wicket and gets a boundary.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
On middle and leg, watchfully defended.
On middle and leg, flicked away for a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Around off, defended solidly.
Change of pace. Mark Wood comes back on to bowl.
Full and just outside off, worked through square leg for one more.
Full again, eased down to long on for a single.
Full on off, pushed back to the bowler.

FOUR! Not quite where he intended. Short and outside off, Marsh goes back to cut but gets a thickish outside edge which flies just wide of short third man, through backward point and meets the ropes. That is 6 off the first 3 balls, giving Morgan something to think about.
Fuller, around off, calmly tucked through square leg for a run.
Short and outside off, Marsh goes back and punches this down to long off for a single.
Outside off, punched away for a run.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Finch goes back and punches it through point. No one in the deep and that is a boundary.
Short and outside off, punched down to long on for a run.
On middle and leg, flicked away through middle and leg for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Nothing on the Free Hit. Delivered slowly on middle, Marsh looks to play the slog sweep but misses. The ball deflects off his body to short third man.
FREE HIT time!
NO BALL! A high full toss, Finch pulls this through mid-wicket and gets a single.
A short ball, heaved through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Another scoring shot missed. Full and down the leg side, swept to the only man inside the circle at 45.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
A tad short on middle, worked through square leg for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

Put down! Was there an edge? Hot Spot picks it! Excellent bowling from Moeen. He slows this beautifully through the air, around off and gets it to spin in. Finch looks to work it through the leg side but misses. Initially, it seems like it has gone off the pads to Buttler who struggles to collect but nope...

SAFE! So looks were not deceptive in this case. Finch works this through the leg side and takes the single. He then comes back for the second, more so on the insistence of Marsh. The latter seems to be slow and the throw comes in to Moeen who whips the bails off. Ahh... replays slow that Moeen has beaten Marsh... in being the slower one. Marsh was short but Moeen was very slow in taking the bails off. Perhaps he was a shade too far from the stumps. Just in, is Marsh.
Ho ho ho! A run out appeal now! Is Marsh gone? He seems confident... Moeen does not look excited... but looks are not everything...
Moeen Ali is back on. Joe Root is done perhaps, for the innings.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. 3-0-9-2 for Root. Lovely bowling.
Mitchell Marsh comes in now. Australia in trouble right to their roots.

OUT! Soft dismissal! Head, well, has not quite used his surname on this ball. Perhaps a bit harsh, but then you should not be coming down the wicket if you are not confident of playing spin. Comes down the track and tamely pushes it back to the bowler. A simple catch. Nothing ball, nothing shot. Waste of a wicket and time.
On middle and leg, flicked through the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Nicely done. Landed outside off, dabbed to short third man for a boundary!
Full and on middle, Finch looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. A mild LBW appeal, going down. Both, the appeal and the ball.
Full on middle, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
Full on middle, pushed straight to mid on.
It's been driven superbly through the covers.
Full and wide outside off, Travis reaches out to drive but misses.
On middle and leg, clipped through mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and outside off, driven straight to the man at short cover. Nearly carried!

On a length outside off, Head works it off the inner half of the bat through square leg. There is a direct hit at the striker's end and there is a muted appeal for a run out. Has Head done a Hardik Pandya by not grounding his bat? Replays show that he did ground his bat. Recently, Pandya was run out in a Test match against South Africa by failing to ground his bat.
Full on middle, driven through mid off for a single. That over was done and dusted in 1 minute and 55 seconds! Whoosh!
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Full and outside off, Travis looks to drive away from his body and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover. Again, a scoring opportunity missed on a bad ball.
Down the leg side, clipped fine for a single.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a couple.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Fuller, on middle and off, driven sweetly but straight to mid off.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Around off, defended solidly.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. Golden change from Morgan. The man with the golden arm has done it. 2 runs and the massive wicket of Smith.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Travis Head comes out to the middle now.

OUT! Umpire's call it is! Australia do not lose a review but does it matter? They have lost their best ODI batsman. Full and outside off, Smith comes forward and looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. That seems to be out and the umpire agrees, raising the finger slowly. Smith walks over to his partner and after some deliberation, takes the review. Well, Hawk Eye shows the ball to be clipping the top of leg stump which means Smith has to go. Another failure. England on top now, after stifling Australia and picking up two big wickets.
Smith is a goner! But he doesn't think so. He has taken a review against the LBW call. That looks dead.
Around off, good bounce again, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
A touch shortish, the line is around off, Finch hops and works it through square leg for a run.
On middle and leg, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
Joe Root replaces Ali in the attack.
Shortish and outside off, Finch chops it past backward point for a couple of runs.
Smith guides it to third man. The batsmen have run through for a single.

18th ODI fifty for Aaron Finch, fourth against England. He stroked a century in the last game and has carried his form into this game. Short and on middle, Aaron pulls it to deep square leg for one. Australia once again will be hoping for a big one from him.
Shortish and on off, punched to sweeper cover for one.

NOT OUT! No bat involved. It's a delivery landing on the shorter side outside off, Smith shuffled across to work it on the leg side but missed. It brushed his pads after going closely past the inside edge of his bat. The bowler appeals for an lbw while the keeper starts to appeal after catching the ball. Eoin Morgan has a chat with his keeper and then takes the DRS. The replays roll in and it finds no bat. They don't feel the need to check for the lbw which used to be a norm earlier. Anyway, the impact was outside off. England lose their only review.
Shout for an lbw followed by a caught behind! Not given and Eoin Morgan after consulting his keeper, takes the DRS. It's for the catch. Has Smith edged it?
Pitches it full and outside off, Steven Smith plays a flowing cover drive but finds the fielder inside the ring.
Wide! Lands it on a good length outside off, just outside the tramline, Smith allows it through and the umpire exercises his arms.
Liam Plunkett is back on.
Uses his feet a little bit this time and whips it through the gap on the leg side. A single taken as the mid-wicket fielder in the deep does the fielding.
Loopy off spinner on off, Smith gets forward and hits it straight towards mid-wicket.
Another gentle nudge off the pads to square leg to rotate the strike.
Leans forward and works it with soft hands through square leg. A couple taken again and Finch moves to 48!
Short and on middle, Finch turns inside the crease and pulls it through backward square leg for a couple.
Flatter and full on middle and leg, Finch fails to properly time his sweep shot.

Drinks time. It's been a good start by the Aussies, however, they lost the wicket of David Warner. This pitch is looking like a batting beauty and Australia will need a big total to test the English team. The spinners are on at the moment and they are finding it tough to get Moeen Ali away. Adil Rashid is targeted as a result and so far it has paid off. An important middle phase is coming up...
Goes down on one knee and pulls a shortish ball through backward square leg for a run. Tidy over by Adil this time, only 2 runs from it.
Flatter and on off, slower in pace, Finch strokes it off his back foot but straight to the cover fielder again.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Goes on the back foot and punches it to covers.
Flighted and on off, Finch paddle sweeps it but finds short fine leg.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Played to the point region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Full floated outside off, driven off the front foot to covers.
On middle, worked on the leg side for one.

Appeal for a caught behind! Quicker delivery on middle and leg, sliding down, Finch gets across a bit and tries to flick. He fails to make proper connection but it goes off something to the keeper. There is a little deflection and Buttler appeals after collecting the ball. Nothing from the umpire. The replays show it kissed the pads.
Shortish and on middle, pulled towards short fine leg.
Flatter and fuller on middle, easily pushed down to long on for a run.
Forces a full ball down to long on for a run. 19 runs from the two overs of Rashid. He is definitely in the target zone for the Aussie batsmen.
The batsman plays a sweep shot. They pick up a single.

Appeal for an lbw! Not given. A well-disguised googly by Rashid. Landing around off and spinning back into the batsman. Finch fails to read the variation and tries to play it from the crease. Fails to keep it out and is hit on the pads. They put in an unsuccessful appeal. Buttler is of the opinion that it would have missed the leg stump. Rashid tells the same to his skipper who was looking for the referral. The replays show that it's clipping the leg pole.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Flatter and fuller on middle, pushed towards mid-wicket.
SIX! High and handsome! They have decided to target the leggie. This time Steven Smith gives the charge. Runs down to the pitch of the delivery and lofts it nonchalantly over long on for a maximum.
Walks forward to a full ball and knocks it down to long on for a run.
Very full and outside off, Smith drives it to covers. Another dot ball.
Played to the point region by the batsman. No run.
Flighted ball on off, Finch flicks it with the spin through backward square leg and rotates the strike.
Finch has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Rashid quickens his pace and serves it around middle and leg, Finch eases it through backward square leg and collects a couple of runs.

SIX! That's colossal! Rashid tosses it up and lands it full around off, Finch lines himself behind the delivery and smashes it mightily over long on for a biggie. 105m on the radar, that was a big one.
Flatter and on middle, played off the pads to mid-wicket.
Wide! Quicker one going down the leg side, Finch tries to sweep but misses. It deflects off Buttler's pads to the point region. No extra run taken.
Smith is off the mark! The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Flighted ball on middle, pushed down to mid on.
Adil Rashid comes into the attack now.
Fires it in, around leg, Smith fails to flick and it goes behind off his pads. They steal a leg bye.
Turning back into the batsman from outside off, on the shorter side, Smith mistimes his back foot punch back to the bowler.
Skipper Steven Smith walks in next. England taking their own sweet time in setting the field.

OUT! A wicket against the run of play! Moeen slows this one in the air and lands it full just outside off. He gets some away spin as it touches the turf and Warner tries to drive it through the line. He ends up getting a thick outside edge behind and Joe Root at first slip makes no mistake. Moeen has provided the much-needed breakthrough. A disappointed Warner heads back to the pavilion.
Short and outside off, Warner moves back and then has to reach for it. Hits it through point, not much power but it goes through the gap for a couple of runs.
Tossed up ball on middle, it's flicked with the spin past short fine leg for one.
Slight tweak in field. The fielder in the deep moves a bit square.
Flighted and on middle, Warner nudges it behind square leg and scampers across for a single. Wants the second run but his partner ain't ready.
Shortish and on off, Warner jumps and punches it to covers for one.
Helps it off his pads to square leg for a run.

FOUR! Up and just over Woakes at the edge of the mid on region. Plunkett bowls it full and wide outside off, Finch tries heaving it probably over mid-wicket but ends up dragging it off the inner half of the bat. It flies over Woakes' outstretched hands and goes to the boundary. For a moment, Finch's heart would have been in his mouth. He has got dismissed many times dragging his shots. Interestingly, this wasn't even a slower one.
Finally manages to connect one off his pads. Works it to fine leg and rotates the strike.
Lands it on a length around leg, Warner once again fails to work it around and is hit on the thigh pad.
Wide! Going down the leg side, Warner fails to flick and it's wided by the umpire.

Stat - David Warner and Aaron Finch now have 1000 runs between them in ODIs in Australia. Surely, a solid partnership upfront for the Aussies. They are looking good today as well and the hosts will be hoping for a strong platform from them.
Full and around off, Warner pushes it off his front foot to mid off.
Powerplay 2 time! The field will relax a bit as four fielders are now allowed outside the ring.
Strays on the pads, Warner clips it behind square leg and cross. Good beginning by Moeen.
Short again and Warner cuts it off his back foot. Fails to find the gap as he hits it straight to point.
Shortish and on middle, Warner goes back and hits it towards short mid-wicket. Excellent over, so far.
A slip in place for Warner.
Slightly short and on middle, Aaron moves back and works it behind square leg for a run.
Tossed up ball on off, Finch draws forward and defends it back.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Moeen Ali to bowl his offies now.
Fuller outside off, driven to mid off to end the over.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished. Drifting down the leg side, Finch neatly deflects it off his pads to the fine leg fence for a boundary. 50 up for Australia!
Good length ball on middle, Warner helps it to square leg for one.

Interesting! The fielder will feel that he was unlucky to concede runs. A length ball outside off, David dabs it down towards backward point where the fielder dives to stop. A slight fumble but he quickly recovers to parry it to the point fielder. He scores a direct hit at the non-striker's end but Finch made it safely. The ball ricochets towards square leg and the batsmen take a couple of runs. Excellent running.
Straighter in line first up, Finch nudges it off his pads towards short fine leg and they cross for a run.
Liam Plunkett comes into the attack.
Fuller and outside off, driven off the front foot but straight to covers.
Fullish and on middle, Warner drills it down the ground but finds the mid on fielder.
Slower and on off, defended on the off side.
Tickles it off his pads to the leg side for a run.
Sliding down the leg side, Finch tries to flick but misses. It deflects off his pads towards Buttler who collects it. The bowler starts to appeal and then the keeper joins. Nothing from the umpire.
FOUR! This is looking like a batting beauty! No sideways movement and the bowlers are struggling. Finch has once again unfurled a cracking pull shot through mid-wicket.

FOUR! Warner is motoring! Wood overdoes his length this time and bowls it short. Warner anticipates it well and as a result has ample time to execute his pull shot. Connects well and sends it racing to the deep square leg fence. 9 from the over!
FOUR! Muscles that again! Width on offer outside off, Warner hangs back inside the crease and bludgeons it down the ground for a boundary. It reaches the fence in the blink of an eye.
A back foot punch in front of the mid off fielder and they pinch a quick single. Good calling by Finch, he set off as soon as he hit it. Warner trusted his partner and responded.
On a length and around off, it's pushed with an angled bat to backward point.
Presents the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Shortish and on off, defended off the back foot.
Another back foot defense by Warner to end the over.
Gets behind the line and defends it off his back foot.
FOUR! Firmly struck. Woakes pitches it full and around off, Warner latches onto it and drills it past his partner at the other end. No chance for mid off.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Angling down the leg side, Aaron nudges it to deep backward square leg for a run.
A length ball on off, staying a touch low, Finch does well to defend it near his front pad.

FOUR! A length ball outside off, David strokes it through the gap between point and cover-point. It's a great placement by Warner and Roy puts in a good chase from point. He speeds after it and pulls it back just before the rope but it seems he was in contact with the fence while he touched the ball. A boundary given.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
A bit of swing as Woakes goes full with his length. It's around leg and Warner fails to flick it. A stifled appeal for an lbw but nothing doing.
Warner works a length ball on the leg side but fails to find the gap.
Fullish and on middle, Finch pushes it down towards mid on and quickly calls his partner for a run. The fielder has a shy at the other end and Finch quickly shouts - your end, to inform his partner.
A little bit short and on off, Finch punches it from the back foot but finds the cover fielder.
Hits the yorker mark on middle, Warner covers the line and digs it out to cover-point.
A bit short and on off, Finch moves back and turns it through backward square leg for a run.
Lands it full and outside off, Aaron gets on the front foot and pushes it to covers.
Shortish and around off, zipping off the surface at 141 kph, Finch once again allows it through.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Aerial but safe! A length ball on middle, Warner tries to flick but gets a leading edge flying wide of point. A single taken.
Back of a length ball on off, Finch defends it back from the crease.
On the hips and eased through backward square leg for a couple of runs.

FOUR! Another powerful shot by Finch. Once again he is served a short ball around off, this time Aaron pulls it in front of square leg for a boundary. Alex Hales inside the ring tries to catch it but it goes past him before he could.
A touch short and on middle, Warner eases himself back before tucking it through backward square leg for a run.
Back of a length ball on off, Warner goes on his toes as he taps it down in front of cover-point.
Short in length, pulled wide of mid on for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Tonk... shot of a batsman in prime form! Finch stands back to a short ball and muscles his pull shot over mid-wicket for a cracking boundary. Gets off the mark in style.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, holding its line, Finch takes a forward stride before leaving it alone.
Fuller and on middle, Warner hits it off the inner half of the bat to wide mid on. A quick single taken.
Once again Warner is beaten on the push. A bit tentative with his footwork at the moment.
Beaten! Excellent delivery, angling away from the batsman on a good length, Warner pushes inside the line and misses.
Good length delivery on middle, Warner turns it off his pads to the leg side but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Chris Woakes to take the second new ball. He also has a couple of slips in place.
Angling in a shortish ball on middle, Finch works it off his pads to backward square leg. Dot ball to end the over.
This time they steal a run as Warner taps a length ball to covers. Good running between the wickets.
A touch short and on off, Warner plays it down to point.
Miscommunication but safe! Warner tries to tap and run after pushing it towards covers but his partner sends him back. The fielder has a shy at the striker's end but misses.
FOUR! Warner is up and running! Wood bangs in a short ball around middle, Warner swivels and pulls it behind square leg. Fine timing and the fine leg fielder had no chance of cutting it off.
Starts with a back of a length delivery on middle and off, Warner goes on his back foot and defends.

Time to get going. Aaron Finch and David Warner are the Aussie openers. Bright and sunny out there with not a single cloud in the sky. The English team is also taking the field now. Mark Wood to bowl with the first new ball. A couple of slips in place. Here we go...

Toss - The coin toss goes in the favour of Steven Smith this time and AUSTRALIA ELECT TO BAT! They have a couple of new faces in their playing XI - Alex Carey and Jhye Richardson make ODI debuts, replacing unfit Tim Paine and rested Pat Cummins. Also, Cameron White makes a comeback after nearly 3 years as Adam Zampa misses out. England following the old mantra, 'if it ain't broke, don't fix it' and are going unchanged.

The Gabbatoir is all set to host the second ODI between Australia and England. The hosts were beaten black and blue in the last match and will be looking for a comeback today. As Steven Smith mentioned, the Aussies have enough quality in the squad but they need to start playing good cricket in this format. The tourists, on the other hand, will be relieved after registering their first success on this pretty dismal tour for them. It was a comprehensive win over the Kangaroos at the MCG and Eoin Morgan's boys will be aiming to repeat the same today. Hello and welcome everyone. We are expecting a cracking contest. Stay with us for all the updates.
